about_accessibility: SkySense aims to meet WCAG 2.2 at level AA. Every change is checked with axe and Lighthouse, and the pages are tested by hand with the keyboard.
about_accessibility_report: If something gets in your way, tell me on GitHub.
about_data: Forecasts come from Open-Meteo, which combines the models of national weather services. They update every hour.
about_languages: SkySense is available in English, German, Slovak, Hungarian and Spanish. The translations are machine-assisted and still being reviewed.

about_places: Town names and the country whose public holidays are shown come from Nominatim, OpenStreetMap's geocoder; the holidays from Nager.Date.
about_space: The aurora line uses the K-index forecast of NOAA's Space Weather Prediction Center; the moon, planets and eclipses are calculated with Astronomy Engine.
about_what: SkySense answers the questions you actually have about the weather, and says how sure it is.

feature_activities: The best time today and in the next 10 days for a run, a ride, a walk, a hike, a picnic, laundry outside, stargazing or golden hour photos, why each score is what it is, and the good times as a calendar file.
feature_air: Air quality and pollen, shown only when they matter.
feature_answers: Plain answers first: a sentence about the next 24 hours, what to wear, whether you need an umbrella, when it gets dark and how windy it is.
feature_comfort: A setting for people who get cold or warm easily, which moves the ideal temperatures for activities.
feature_confidence: How sure the forecast is: the likely range from 51 runs of the ECMWF model, marks on uncertain days, and five weather models side by side.
feature_normal: How today compares with 1991 to 2020, unusual or not, this date in recent years, how dry it has been, any past day since 1940, and the change since 1961.
feature_offline: Installs as an app, and shows places you opened before when you are offline.
feature_places: Places you can save, rename, reorder and back up to a file, a "My location" entry that finds you again when opened, two places compared day by day, a search in your language, and a link to share any place.
feature_radar: A rain radar for the last 2 hours and the model's rain for the next 3, on a map, with its temperature and wind too.
feature_settings: Your units, 12 or 24-hour time, a light or dark theme or one that follows the weather, and five languages.
feature_sky: Tonight's moon, when it rises and sets, the next full moon and meteor showers, sunrise and sunset, the barometer and whether it is rising or falling, and a background sky that follows the time of day and the weather.

pick_on_map_help: Move the map until the pin is on the spot: drag it or tap a point, or use the arrow keys and + and −. Enter takes the spot.
privacy_radar: The rain radar map loads its images straight from RainViewer (radar), CARTO (map) and, for the satellite picture, NASA GIBS, so they see your IP address and the area you look at.
privacy_reverse: When you use your location or pick a spot on the map, our server also asks OpenStreetMap's Nominatim service for the name of the town there. For every place, it asks Nominatim which country it is in, with the coordinates rounded to about 10 km, and Nager.Date for that country's public holidays, sending only the country. Both see our server, not you.

privacy_device: Saved places, your settings and your chosen activities are stored on this device only, in local storage and cookies. Clearing your browser data removes them.
privacy_hosting: SkySense runs on Vercel, which keeps short-lived request logs, including IP addresses, to operate the service. There is no analytics.
privacy_location: When you use your location or open a place, its coordinates are rounded to about 1 km and sent to our server, which asks Open-Meteo for the forecast. Open-Meteo only ever sees our server, not you. Our server keeps the forecast for a rounded place in memory for a few minutes, not linked to you.
privacy_summary: No accounts, no tracking, no ads.
